metadata.scope: Comprehensive security audit covering web, runner, and Python backend
metadata.methodology: Static code analysis, pattern matching, architecture review

vulnerabilities.description: API credentials stored in sessionStorage, accessible to JavaScript
vulnerabilities.proof: Lines 21-24 define INTERVALS_KEY and STRAVA_KEY for sessionStorage; line 26 tries to migrate from localStorage but tokens persist during session
vulnerabilities.impact: XSS vulnerabilities could exfiltrate API tokens; malicious scripts can access tokens directly from sessionStorage; tokens visible in browser DevTools memory
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use httpOnly cookies for API tokens; implement server-side session storage; use short-lived tokens with refresh mechanism; consider OAuth flow instead of static tokens

vulnerabilities.description: API keys transmitted in Base64-encoded Authorization headers (equivalent to plaintext)
vulnerabilities.proof: Authorization: Basic ${btoa(`API_KEY:${apiKey}`)} — Base64 is not encryption; keys visible in browser memory, network logs, and DevTools
vulnerabilities.impact: API keys are easily decoded from Authorization headers; exposed in browser history, request logs, and memory dumps; could be captured by network sniffing proxies
vulnerabilities.remediation: Implement server-side OAuth token exchange; never store API keys in browser; use secure httpOnly cookies for authenticated requests; implement PKCE flow for public clients

vulnerabilities.description: Race condition in Garmin MFA completion check allows concurrent login attempts
vulnerabilities.proof: Line 300 checks if _GARMIN_CLIENT is None after garmin_login_start() has already started a daemon thread. If garmin_mfa() is called before login completes, or multiple MFA attempts are made, the state machine breaks
vulnerabilities.impact: Attacker could trigger multiple concurrent MFA attempts; could bypass MFA by calling garmin_mfa() with multiple codes in parallel; _GARMIN_CLIENT could be null-checked after deletion
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use threading.Lock() to serialize Garmin login/MFA state transitions; replace global _GARMIN_CLIENT with a queue; validate login state more strictly before accepting MFA

vulnerabilities.description: Direct innerHTML assignment with potentially unsanitized content
vulnerabilities.proof: Lines 159, 282, 433, 515, 699, 818, 870 all use .innerHTML = . While many use static strings or escHtml(), some dynamic values from user data could bypass escaping
vulnerabilities.impact: If dynamic content from workouts, ride names, or user input reaches innerHTML without escaping, XSS is possible; could execute arbitrary JavaScript
vulnerabilities.remediation: Always use escHtml() for all user-controlled content; prefer textContent over innerHTML; use template literals with escaping helpers; use DOMParser for complex HTML

vulnerabilities.description: Insufficient validation of bike ride trace data bounds
vulnerabilities.proof: Lines 378-379 validate that sec (0-86400) and watts (0-3000) are in range, but watts upper bound of 3000W is arbitrary and doesn't validate against rider's FTP or equipment capabilities
vulnerabilities.impact: Malicious trace data could corrupt load calculations; invalid wattage values could skew training analysis; could be used to trigger integer overflow in downstream calculations
vulnerabilities.remediation: Validate trace points against athlete's FTP; implement reasonable bounds based on FTP (e.g., max 6x FTP for elite riders); add CRC checksum to trace data

vulnerabilities.description: JSON data files world-readable (mode 664) containing training history and personal metrics
vulnerabilities.proof: All data/*.json files have permissions 664 (rw-rw-r--): readable by any user on the system
vulnerabilities.impact: Other users on shared system can read training data, heart rate history, race times, fitness metrics, and Garmin sync status
vulnerabilities.remediation: Change file permissions to 600 (owner only) or 640 (owner + group); enforce umask(0077) on file creation; consider encrypting sensitive data at rest

vulnerabilities.description: Bitwise operators used instead of logical operators in auth check, reducing code clarity and maintainability
vulnerabilities.proof: Line 818: user_ok = hmac.compare_digest(...) | (bool(email) & hmac.compare_digest(...)) — uses | and & instead of or/and; while functionally correct, semantically confusing
vulnerabilities.impact: Code difficult to understand; future refactoring might introduce logical errors; someone might accidentally short-circuit the timing-safe comparison
vulnerabilities.remediation: Replace bitwise operators with logical operators; use all() or any() for clarity; add comments explaining the OR logic for username vs email acceptance

vulnerabilities.description: Garmin password stored in process memory during login, potentially exposed if process crashes or memory is dumped
vulnerabilities.proof: Line 262: client = GarminClient(email, password, ...) creates a client holding the plaintext password; stored in _GARMIN_CLIENT global during login retry loop (line 287 sleeps up to 45 min)
vulnerabilities.impact: If process crashes with core dump, password is recoverable; if process is debugged, password is visible; potential memory scraping if process is compromised
vulnerabilities.remediation: Clear password from memory after initial login attempt; use secure strings that zero on deletion; implement immediate token persistence and discard password; consider using OAuth with device flow

vulnerabilities.description: Generic JSON.parse error handling could mask parsing issues and hide malformed data
vulnerabilities.proof: Lines 662, 795, 803, 1403, 1919 use try/catch with JSON.parse, returning fallback without logging the error
vulnerabilities.impact: Silent failures when data is corrupted; difficult to debug parsing issues; could hide data tampering or cache corruption
vulnerabilities.remediation: Log parse errors to console or error reporting service; validate schema after parsing; use JSON schema validation library

vulnerabilities.description: No explicit CORS or security headers set on HTTP responses
vulnerabilities.proof: The _send() method (line 867) doesn't set X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy, or CORS headers
vulnerabilities.impact: Reduces defense-in-depth; doesn't prevent clickjacking or content-sniffing attacks; relies entirely on same-origin policy (which works for this app but is fragile)
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add security headers: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self', X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block

vulnerabilities.description: Numeric entity parsing could overflow JavaScript number range
vulnerabilities.proof: Lines 26-31 parse numeric entities ({ or «) without checking if the parsed code point is valid Unicode or within safe bounds
vulnerabilities.impact: Parsing `&#99999999;` could result in invalid characters; no validation that resulting character is valid; edge case but could cause downstream issues
vulnerabilities.remediation: Validate numeric entities are within valid Unicode range (0x10FFFF); reject surrogates; skip undefined code points gracefully

architectural_findings.finding: Garmin token stored on disk (~1 year expiration); Portal credentials in .env file (scrypt hash, but still sensitive)
architectural_findings.details: Token refresh happens on every sync (good), but if token is compromised, no mechanism to invalidate it; scrypt hash is strong but env vars could be exposed via process listing or container inspection
architectural_findings.recommendation: Implement token revocation mechanism; consider using OS credential store (Keychain/Windows Credential Manager) instead of filesystem; rotate token if possible

architectural_findings.finding: Single login per instance; no logout mechanism; no multi-factor authentication on portal login
architectural_findings.details: Session TTL is 180 days (very long); no refresh token pattern; compromised session cookie grants 6 months of access
architectural_findings.recommendation: Reduce SESSION_TTL to 7-30 days; implement refresh token pattern; add logout endpoint; consider adding optional TOTP/U2F

architectural_findings.finding: RPE, benchmarks, and event entries accept minimal validation; trace data from bike rides accepts arbitrary point values
architectural_findings.details: No upper bounds on string lengths for notes (500 chars is OK), but no schema validation; bike profile FTP accepts 50-600W (reasonable but could accept 1000W with portal manipulation)
architectural_findings.recommendation: Implement Pydantic models for all JSON input; validate against schema; add audit log for data mutations; implement idempotency checks

architectural_findings.finding: Job dispatch accepts arbitrary string inputs without strict schema validation
architectural_findings.details: Coach requests accept free-form title+body; plan creation accepts level/event strings; inputs are passed to subprocess as env vars or command args (which is safe) but no schema validation
architectural_findings.recommendation: Create Pydantic models for each job's inputs; validate enum fields (level, event_type) against whitelist; sanitize free-text inputs before logging

positive_findings: Path traversal protection is solid: is_relative_to() checks prevent directory traversal
Subprocess calls use fixed argument lists, not string interpolation (safe from command injection)
Session cookies use HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite flags (secure cookie handling)
Passwords use scrypt hashing with strong parameters (n=2^14, r=8, p=1)
XML parser is custom and safe from XXE (skips DOCTYPE, no entity expansion)
File upload size capped at 1 MiB (prevents memory exhaustion)
Login brute-force mitigation: 1 second delay per failed attempt
Garmin credentials never logged; held only in memory during handshake
testing_recommendations: Add security-focused unit tests: auth bypass, race conditions, injection attacks
Implement secrets scanning in CI/CD to prevent credential commits
Add input validation tests for all API endpoints
Test race conditions in Garmin login flow with concurrent requests
Verify sessionStorage tokens are cleared on logout/session expiry
Test XSS protection by injecting HTML/JS into all text input fields
Verify HTTPS enforcement and certificate pinning for Garmin/external APIs
Add penetration testing for job dispatch parameters

risk_score_rationale: Medium risk overall. No critical vulnerabilities but several medium-severity issues around credential storage (sessionStorage/Basic Auth API keys) and race conditions in auth flow. Data validation and auth logic are generally solid. File permissions and lack of security headers are low-risk but easy wins. Risk is mitigated by design: single-user system, local network, limited attack surface.

recommendations.title: Move API tokens to server-side session storage
recommendations.description: Implement server-side OAuth token exchange instead of storing intervals.icu and Strava tokens in sessionStorage. Store tokens in secure httpOnly cookies instead.

recommendations.title: Fix Garmin MFA race condition
recommendations.description: Replace global _GARMIN_CLIENT with a thread-safe queue/state machine. Use locks to serialize login state transitions.

recommendations.title: Implement consistent XSS protection
recommendations.description: Audit all innerHTML assignments in web/bike/view.js. Replace with textContent or use consistent escHtml() wrapper.

recommendations.title: Add security headers
recommendations.description: Set X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, CSP, and other protective headers on all HTTP responses.

recommendations.title: Secure file permissions
recommendations.description: Change data/*.json to mode 600 (owner only) or 640 (owner + group). Enforce umask(0077) on file creation.

recommendations.title: Reduce session TTL
recommendations.description: Change SESSION_TTL from 180 days to 7-30 days. Implement refresh token pattern.

recommendations.title: Clear Garmin password from memory
recommendations.description: Zero password after initial login attempt. Discard password immediately, don't keep in client for retries.

recommendations.title: Add input validation schema
recommendations.description: Create Pydantic models for all job inputs and JSON payloads. Validate enums and string lengths.
